A 'culprit' verdict would imply a perpetrator identification that the case files do not support.)

translations.t0087: During the night of Friday 10 to Saturday 11 October 2025, MERIDIAN model artefacts (checkpoint bundles and corpus manifest) were copied from the scratch array scratch-02 — which is not connected to the audit pipeline — to an externally attached portable block device. Audit logging was scheduled to be disabled (ticket INFRA-2291, window 21:00 Friday to 06:00 Saturday). A first copy attempt failed at approximately 40% because the target device was full; after deleting an old snapshot (~9.1 TB), the task was restarted from the beginning and completed successfully at 03:52 UTC (05:52 CEST). The device was disconnected at 03:58 UTC. None of the eleven decoy bundles was opened, indicating prior knowledge of the genuine artefacts.
translations.t0088: The forensic report (Bakalian) works in UTC; local CEST time is UTC+2. Job start 21:10 UTC = 23:10 CEST; device disconnection 03:58 UTC = 05:58 CEST. Logging window per INFRA-2291: 21:00 Friday to 06:00 Saturday local time, i.e. 19:00–04:00 UTC.
translations.t0089: Audit logging (collector and SIEM cold tier) was scheduled to be disabled for the window Friday 21:00 to Saturday 06:00 local time (ticket INFRA-2291).
translations.t0090: A bulk copy job started at 21:10 UTC (23:10 CEST) on scratch-02 and wrote MERIDIAN checkpoint bundles and the corpus manifest to an externally attached portable block device.
translations.t0091: The first run failed at approximately 40% because the checkpoint bundles decompress on write and filled the target device; at 00:41 UTC an older snapshot was deleted (~9.1 TB freed), and at 00:44 UTC the job was restarted from the beginning.
translations.t0092: The second run completed successfully at 03:52 UTC (05:52 CEST); the device was disconnected at 03:58 UTC — eight minutes before logging was restored.
translations.t0093: Not a single one of the eleven decoy bundles was opened; the genuine artefacts were copied selectively, which presupposes perpetrator knowledge of the distinction.
